messages.subject: Sampling for a local variable
parts:
Hi all,

I am using Stan to implement an algorithm for a novel model.  What I need is a temporal categorical variable generated from  a distribution.
Apparently, integer variables are not supportive in parameters block. The only choice left is to create a local variable in model block.

To show my intention, here is code.

Then I tried to sample for a local variable s in the model block

fit <- stan(file = 'localVar.stan', iter = 1, chains = 1)

I got the error:

left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:


It seems that it is impossible to sample for a local variable in model block, except for the variables defined in the data block and parameters block.
If it is the case, is there alternative to save a temporal value generated from a distribution in model block?

Any ideas will be highly appreciated.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sampling for a local variable
parts:
You might want to have a look at the manual and other models
in Stan before attempting to write one yourself. It doesn't
work like BUGS.

The warning you cite is just that --- a warning. But
your code is missing parameter declarations, so there's nothing
that would be saved even if it did run. The ~ doesn't do
random number generation; it just increments the log density.
Also when it is called in that Stan program, s wouldn't be defined.

Stan does not support integer parameters directly. You
need to marginalize them out.

If the temporal categorical variable is finite, you probably
have something like a hidden Markov model (aka state-space
model). There's a chapter in the manual explaining how to do HMMs
and the latent discrete parameter chapter explains how to deal with
a custom ecology state-space model.

- Bob
